welcome.p1.title: Welcome to Kinobu
welcome.p1.body: Kinobu is an advanced customisation of Ubuntu built for working with artificial intelligence. It is more than a new desktop: it sets up the system, the apps, the agents, the shortcuts and the look so that everything works together from the first minute. Ubuntu is still underneath, with its updates and all its software.
welcome.p2.title: Why Kinobu
welcome.p2.body: Installing an AI agent is easy. Truly integrating it into the system is not: it has to be set up to measure, and almost nothing gives you that done, and done well. Kinobu does it for you, with the most popular agents at once and the tools you use every day. The idea comes from Omarchy, DHH's system. Kinobu invents nothing: it brings what has already proven to work to a more stable base. Omarchy bets on customising everything; Kinobu, on a stable, practical system for work.
welcome.p3.title: Why Ubuntu
welcome.p3.body: Work needs a system that just works every day, not the very latest of everything. Fedora renews itself every six months and Arch Linux updates non-stop; Arch also has a huge community repository (the AUR). But every jump of GNOME can break part of the customisation, such as the extensions. Ubuntu is maintained by a company, Canonical, with long-term support releases that keep the same desktop for years, and many professional apps are published for it officially. It is the ideal base for professional work.
welcome.p4.title: A desktop you already know
welcome.p4.body: Kinobu uses GNOME because it is intuitive, visual and easy to follow. KDE Plasma is very complete, but it is easy to get lost in its options, and making it look good takes a lot of setting up. Hyprland is very technical: you would learn to use a desktop you would only use there. Kinobu uses what you already know: the beauty of macOS, the shortcuts of Windows and the virtual desktops of Linux, without what gets in the way. The dock at the bottom, 4 workspaces with their own wallpaper and a compact top bar with the clock, the weather, the clipboard and your notifications.
welcome.p5.title: Your agents, always at hand
welcome.p5.body: Super+Shift+Enter opens your agent in a terminal. While it works, it tells you when it finishes, when it is waiting for you or when it needs your permission, so you do not have to keep an eye on it. It knows your system thanks to the Kinobu skill.
welcome.p5.voice: With Super+Space you can talk to it.
welcome.p5.none: No agent is installed yet: add one with <tt>kinobu.sh --install</tt>.
welcome.p6.title: The shortcuts you will use most
welcome.p6.body: If you come from Windows, you already know them. Kinobu includes most of its shortcuts, because they are the ones almost everybody uses every day, and adds a few of its own for what Windows does not have. The Super key is the Windows key.
welcome.p7.title: All set
welcome.p7.body: Just a few steps to make it yours:
welcome.p7.google.mail: Your mail in Geary, which tells you about new mail even when closed, plus your contacts, calendar and Google Drive, all built into the system.
welcome.p7.google.nomail: Your contacts, calendar and Google Drive, all built into the system.
welcome.p7.handy.sub: We recommend Parakeet Ultra: it transcribes best and runs well on any reasonably capable computer. Handy uses your default microphone; if it does not hear you, pick it in its settings.
welcome.p7.update.sub: <tt>kinobu.sh --update</tt> updates the system and Kinobu without touching your look.
welcome.p7.again: You can see this welcome again from the app grid.
welcome.p5.assistant: With Super+Shift+Space you talk to Willow, the voice assistant: it answers aloud and hands bigger jobs to your agent.

voice.tier_kokoro: Natural: a recent processor is enough
voice.tier_qwen: The most natural: a graphics card is recommended
voice.hint_muted: Unmute it with the button, Ctrl+M or Super+Alt+K
voice.sound_off: Sound is muted: I answer in writing
voice.no_agent: I can't find your agent. For now I work with Claude Code: install it and sign in.
voice.agent_error: Your agent did not answer. Check that it is signed in.
voice.no_voice: My voice could not start: I answer in writing.
voice.a1: Hi, I'm Kinobu's receptionist. Today is Wednesday, the eleventh of November, and you have two meetings in the afternoon. Shall I open the project in the terminal?
voice.a2: Done. Claude Code is opening the project for you.
voice.typed: This is the demo: typed messages get a canned answer for now.
voice.sample: Voice test. Tomorrow, Saturday, you have a dentist appointment at 11:30. Have you brushed your teeth? Don't forget!
voice.ref_text: Hello there. I'm here to help you with your day: your plans, your questions and the little things on your computer. Just ask, and we'll work it out together.
voice.background_failed: The background check could not be finished
voice.power_quick_note: Haiku, low effort: fast and cheap
voice.power_strong_note: Sonnet, medium effort: slower, uses more
voice.restarted: New settings: the talk starts afresh

notify.countdown: No answer: the terminal decides in %s s

seasons.intro: Choose how your desktop looks. A theme changes everything at once: the colour of your apps, the icons, the cursor, the window buttons, the terminal and the wallpapers. Each theme has its palettes, dark or light: pick one with the round buttons. Apps that are open take it when you open them again.
seasons.applied: {name} is ready. Apps that are open change when you open them again.
seasons.icons_intro: The icons of your apps and folders.
seasons.fonts_intro: The letters of the desktop and of the apps.
seasons.wallpapers_intro: Four wallpapers, one per workspace. With more workspaces they repeat in order.
seasons.monospace_font_desc: Text editors and code. The terminal keeps its own font, which has the prompt's symbols
seasons.sample: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
seasons.follow_icons: The theme chooses the icons. Turn it off to pick your own: they stay when you change themes.
